title: 10. NLP, Transformers & LLMs: Naive Bayes for Text Classification
summary: Goal: Master Naive Bayes - the fastest and simplest text classifier.

sections.title: Why Naive Bayes?
sections.body:
**Goal**: Master Naive Bayes - the fastest and simplest text classifier.

### Advantages
```
✓ EXTREMELY fast (training & prediction)
✓ Works well with small datasets
✓ Handles high-dimensional data naturally
✓ Probabilistic predictions
✓ Strong baseline for text
✓ Often hard to beat on spam detection!
```

### The "Naive" Assumption
```
Assumes features are INDEPENDENT given the class.

Example:
P("good" and "movie" | positive) = P("good" | positive) × P("movie" | positive)

This is "naive" because words are often dependent:
• "not good" ≠ "good"
• "machine learning" is a phrase

But it works surprisingly well anyway!
```

sections.title: Bayes' Theorem Refresher
sections.body:
$$
P(class|document) = \frac{P(document|class) \times P(class)}{P(document)}
$$

**In practice**:
```
P(spam | email) = P(email | spam) × P(spam) / P(email)
                  ↓                 ↓          ↓
              Likelihood        Prior    Evidence (ignored)
```

**For classification**, we compare:
```
P(positive | review) vs P(negative | review)
```

Pick the class with higher probability!

sections.title: Three Variants
sections.body:
### 1. Multinomial Naive Bayes
```
• For COUNT data (word frequencies)
• Best with BoW or TF-IDF
• Most common for text
```

### 2. Bernoulli Naive Bayes
```
• For BINARY data (word present/absent)
• Useful for short texts
• Considers absence of words
```

### 3. Gaussian Naive Bayes
```
• For CONTINUOUS data
• Rarely used for text
• Better for numeric features
```

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer, TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.naive_bayes import MultinomialNB, BernoulliNB, GaussianNB
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split, cross_val_score
from sklearn.metrics import classification_report, confusion_matrix, accuracy_score
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
import time

sns.set_style('whitegrid')
plt.rcParams['figure.figsize'] = (12, 6)
np.random.seed(42)
```

sections.title: Dataset: Spam vs Ham Emails
sections.body:
```python
# Email dataset
emails = [
    # Spam emails
    "Win $1000 cash prize! Click here NOW to claim your money!",
    "FREE VIAGRA! Order now without prescription! Limited offer!",
    "You've won the lottery! Send your bank details to claim prize!",
    "Make $$$ working from home! No experience needed! Act now!",
    "URGENT: Your account will be closed! Verify identity immediately!",
    "Get rich quick! Earn thousands per week! Click here!",
    "Congratulations! You're selected for amazing offer! Order today!",
    "FREE iPhone! Just pay shipping! Limited stock! Hurry!",
    "Lose weight fast! Amazing pills! 100% guaranteed results!",
    "Prize notification! Claim your free gift card now!",
    # Ham emails
    "Hi John, can we schedule a meeting for tomorrow afternoon?",
    "The quarterly report is attached. Please review before Friday.",
    "Thanks for your email. I'll get back to you by end of day.",
    "Meeting rescheduled to 3pm in conference room B.",
    "Please find the updated project timeline in the attachment.",
    "Let me know if you have any questions about the proposal.",
    "I've completed the review and sent my feedback.",
    "Can you send me the latest version of the presentation?",
    "The team meeting is confirmed for next Tuesday.",
    "I'll be out of office next week. Please contact Sarah.",
] * 20  # Replicate for larger dataset

labels = ([1] * 10 + [0] * 10) * 20  # 1=spam, 0=ham

print(f"📊 Dataset: {len(emails)} emails")
print(f"   Spam: {sum(labels)} ({sum(labels)/len(labels)*100:.0f}%)")
print(f"   Ham:  {len(labels) - sum(labels)} ({(len(labels) - sum(labels))/len(labels)*100:.0f}%)")
print()
print("Sample emails:")
for i in [0, 10]:  # First spam and first ham
    label_str = "SPAM" if labels[i] == 1 else "HAM"
    print(f"  [{label_str}] {emails[i]}")
```

sections.title: Train-Test Split
sections.body:
```python
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    emails, labels, test_size=0.25, random_state=42, stratify=labels
)

print("📊 Data Split:")
print(f"   Training: {len(X_train)} emails")
print(f"   Test:     {len(X_test)} emails")
```

sections.title: Multinomial Naive Bayes (with BoW)
sections.body:
```python
# Create pipeline: CountVectorizer + MultinomialNB
mnb_pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('vectorizer', CountVectorizer()),
    ('classifier', MultinomialNB())
])

# Train
start_time = time.time()
mnb_pipeline.fit(X_train, y_train)
train_time = time.time() - start_time

# Predict
start_time = time.time()
y_pred = mnb_pipeline.predict(X_test)
predict_time = time.time() - start_time

# Evaluate
accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)

print("🎯 Multinomial Naive Bayes Performance:")
print(f"   Training time:   {train_time*1000:.2f} ms")
print(f"   Prediction time: {predict_time*1000:.2f} ms")
print(f"   Accuracy:        {accuracy:.3f}")
print()
print("📋 Classification Report:")
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred, target_names=['Ham', 'Spam']))
```

sections.title: Understanding Probabilities
sections.body:
```python
# Get probability predictions
y_pred_proba = mnb_pipeline.predict_proba(X_test)

# Show examples with probabilities
print("🔮 Prediction Examples with Probabilities:")
print()
for i in range(5):
    true_label = "SPAM" if y_test[i] == 1 else "HAM"
    pred_label = "SPAM" if y_pred[i] == 1 else "HAM"
    prob_ham = y_pred_proba[i][0]
    prob_spam = y_pred_proba[i][1]
    
    print(f"{i+1}. Email: \"{X_test[i][:60]}...\"")
    print(f"   True: {true_label} | Predicted: {pred_label}")
    print(f"   P(Ham)={prob_ham:.4f}, P(Spam)={prob_spam:.4f}")
    print()
```

sections.title: Feature Log Probabilities
sections.body:
```python
# Get feature names and log probabilities
vectorizer = mnb_pipeline.named_steps['vectorizer']
classifier = mnb_pipeline.named_steps['classifier']

feature_names = vectorizer.get_feature_names_out()
log_prob_ham = classifier.feature_log_prob_[0]  # Class 0 (ham)
log_prob_spam = classifier.feature_log_prob_[1]  # Class 1 (spam)

# Create DataFrame
prob_df = pd.DataFrame({
    'word': feature_names,
    'log_prob_ham': log_prob_ham,
    'log_prob_spam': log_prob_spam,
    'spam_ham_ratio': np.exp(log_prob_spam - log_prob_ham)
})

# Top spam indicators
top_spam = prob_df.nlargest(15, 'spam_ham_ratio')
print("🔴 Top 15 Spam Indicators:")
print()
for idx, row in top_spam.iterrows():
    print(f"   {row['word']:15s}  spam/ham ratio: {row['spam_ham_ratio']:8.2f}x")

# Top ham indicators
top_ham = prob_df.nsmallest(15, 'spam_ham_ratio')
print("\n🟢 Top 15 Ham Indicators:")
print()
for idx, row in top_ham.iterrows():
    print(f"   {row['word']:15s}  spam/ham ratio: {row['spam_ham_ratio']:8.2f}x")
```

```python
# Visualize spam vs ham word probabilities
top_words = prob_df.nlargest(10, 'spam_ham_ratio')

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
x = np.arange(len(top_words))
width = 0.35

ax.bar(x - width/2, np.exp(top_words['log_prob_spam']), width, label='Spam', color='red', alpha=0.7)
ax.bar(x + width/2, np.exp(top_words['log_prob_ham']), width, label='Ham', color='green', alpha=0.7)

ax.set_xlabel('Words')
ax.set_ylabel('Probability')
ax.set_title('Word Probabilities: Spam vs Ham')
ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels(top_words['word'], rotation=45, ha='right')
ax.legend()
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3, axis='y')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

sections.title: Compare: Multinomial vs Bernoulli Naive Bayes
sections.body:
```python
# Bernoulli Naive Bayes (binary features)
bnb_pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('vectorizer', CountVectorizer(binary=True)),  # Binary: word present or not
    ('classifier', BernoulliNB())
])

bnb_pipeline.fit(X_train, y_train)
bnb_pred = bnb_pipeline.predict(X_test)
bnb_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, bnb_pred)

print("🆚 Comparison: Multinomial vs Bernoulli")
print()
print(f"Multinomial NB Accuracy: {accuracy:.3f}")
print(f"Bernoulli NB Accuracy:   {bnb_accuracy:.3f}")
print()
print("💡 Difference:")
print("   • Multinomial: Uses word COUNTS (\"free\" appears 3 times)")
print("   • Bernoulli:   Uses word PRESENCE (\"free\" appears: yes/no)")
```

sections.title: Hyperparameter: Alpha (Smoothing)
sections.body:
```python
# Test different alpha values
alphas = [0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0]
train_scores = []
test_scores = []

vectorizer = CountVectorizer()
X_train_vec = vectorizer.fit_transform(X_train)
X_test_vec = vectorizer.transform(X_test)

for alpha in alphas:
    model = MultinomialNB(alpha=alpha)
    model.fit(X_train_vec, y_train)
    train_scores.append(model.score(X_train_vec, y_train))
    test_scores.append(model.score(X_test_vec, y_test))

# Plot
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.semilogx(alphas, train_scores, 'o-', label='Training accuracy', linewidth=2)
plt.semilogx(alphas, test_scores, 's-', label='Test accuracy', linewidth=2)
plt.xlabel('Alpha (Laplace smoothing parameter)')
plt.ylabel('Accuracy')
plt.title('Effect of Alpha on Naive Bayes Performance')
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("\n💡 Alpha (Laplace Smoothing):")
print("   • Handles words not seen during training")
print("   • alpha=1.0 (default): Add 1 to all word counts")
print("   • alpha=0.0: No smoothing (not recommended!)")
print("   • Higher alpha → More smoothing → Simpler model")
```

sections.title: Speed Comparison: NB vs Logistic Regression
sections.body:
```python
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

# Prepare data
vectorizer = CountVectorizer()
X_train_vec = vectorizer.fit_transform(X_train)
X_test_vec = vectorizer.transform(X_test)

# Naive Bayes
nb_model = MultinomialNB()
start = time.time()
nb_model.fit(X_train_vec, y_train)
nb_train_time = time.time() - start
start = time.time()
nb_model.predict(X_test_vec)
nb_predict_time = time.time() - start
nb_accuracy = nb_model.score(X_test_vec, y_test)

# Logistic Regression
lr_model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000, random_state=42)
start = time.time()
lr_model.fit(X_train_vec, y_train)
lr_train_time = time.time() - start
start = time.time()
lr_model.predict(X_test_vec)
lr_predict_time = time.time() - start
lr_accuracy = lr_model.score(X_test_vec, y_test)

# Comparison
print("⚡ Speed Comparison:")
print()
print(f"{'Model':<20s} {'Train Time':>12s} {'Predict Time':>14s} {'Accuracy':>10s}")
print("-" * 60)
print(f"{'Naive Bayes':<20s} {nb_train_time*1000:>10.2f} ms {nb_predict_time*1000:>12.2f} ms {nb_accuracy:>10.3f}")
print(f"{'Logistic Regression':<20s} {lr_train_time*1000:>10.2f} ms {lr_predict_time*1000:>12.2f} ms {lr_accuracy:>10.3f}")
print()
print(f"💡 Naive Bayes is {lr_train_time/nb_train_time:.1f}x FASTER at training!")
print(f"💡 Naive Bayes is {lr_predict_time/nb_predict_time:.1f}x FASTER at prediction!")
```

sections.title: Real-World Example: News Topic Classification
sections.body:
```python
# Multi-class classification: news topics
news_articles = [
    # Technology
    "Apple releases new iPhone with improved camera and processor.",
    "AI startup raises $50 million in Series B funding round.",
    "Google announces breakthrough in quantum computing research.",
    "Microsoft launches new cloud services for enterprise customers.",
    "Tesla unveils autonomous driving software update.",
    # Sports
    "Lakers win championship in overtime thriller against Celtics.",
    "Cristiano Ronaldo scores hat-trick in Champions League final.",
    "Olympic Games opening ceremony attracts record viewership.",
    "Tennis star advances to Wimbledon finals after tough match.",
    "NFL draft: Top quarterback picked by struggling franchise.",
    # Politics
    "Senate passes bipartisan infrastructure bill after months of debate.",
    "Presidential candidate leads in latest national polls.",
    "Supreme Court rules on landmark voting rights case.",
    "Congress holds hearing on economic recovery plan.",
    "Governor announces new education funding initiative.",
] * 20

topics = ([0] * 5 + [1] * 5 + [2] * 5) * 20  # 0=tech, 1=sports, 2=politics

# Train-test split
X_train_news, X_test_news, y_train_news, y_test_news = train_test_split(
    news_articles, topics, test_size=0.25, random_state=42, stratify=topics
)

# Train multi-class Naive Bayes
news_pipeline = Pipeline([
    ('tfidf', TfidfVectorizer(max_features=200)),
    ('clf', MultinomialNB())
])

news_pipeline.fit(X_train_news, y_train_news)
news_pred = news_pipeline.predict(X_test_news)
news_accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test_news, news_pred)

print("📰 News Topic Classification:")
print(f"   Accuracy: {news_accuracy:.3f}")
print()
print("📋 Classification Report:")
print(classification_report(
    y_test_news, news_pred,
    target_names=['Technology', 'Sports', 'Politics']
))
```

```python
# Confusion matrix
cm = confusion_matrix(y_test_news, news_pred)

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.heatmap(cm, annot=True, fmt='d', cmap='Blues',
            xticklabels=['Tech', 'Sports', 'Politics'],
            yticklabels=['Tech', 'Sports', 'Politics'])
plt.ylabel('True Label')
plt.xlabel('Predicted Label')
plt.title('Confusion Matrix: News Topic Classification')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

sections.title: Make Predictions on New Articles
sections.body:
```python
# New articles to classify
new_articles = [
    "Amazon announces new data center for cloud computing services.",
    "Basketball team wins playoff game with buzzer-beater shot.",
    "Mayor proposes new tax policy for city budget.",
]

# Predict
predictions = news_pipeline.predict(new_articles)
probabilities = news_pipeline.predict_proba(new_articles)

topic_names = ['Technology', 'Sports', 'Politics']

print("🔮 Predictions on New Articles:")

for article, pred, proba in zip(new_articles, predictions, probabilities):
    print(f"Article: \"{article}\"")
    print(f"  → Predicted: {topic_names[pred]}")
    print(f"  → Probabilities:")
    for i, topic in enumerate(topic_names):
        print(f"      {topic:12s}: {proba[i]:.3f}")
    print()
```

sections.title: Summary: Naive Bayes
sections.body:
### Key Advantages
```
✓ Extremely fast (training & prediction)
✓ Works well with small datasets
✓ Handles high-dimensional data
✓ Simple and interpretable
✓ Great baseline model
✓ Often surprisingly effective!
```

### When to Use
```
✓ Spam detection
✓ Document classification
✓ Sentiment analysis
✓ Real-time classification
✓ Need fast baseline
✓ Small training data
```

### Limitations
```
✗ Independence assumption (words are dependent!)
✗ Can't capture word order
✗ Struggles with feature interactions
✗ May underperform on complex tasks
```

### Variants
```python
MultinomialNB()   # For count data (BoW, TF-IDF)
BernoulliNB()     # For binary data (word present/absent)
GaussianNB()      # For continuous data (rarely used for text)
```

### Important Parameter
```python
alpha=1.0  # Laplace smoothing
           # Handles unseen words
           # Higher = more smoothing
```

### Pro Tip
```
Always try Naive Bayes first!
• Fast to train
• Strong baseline
• Hard to beat on some tasks (spam!)
• If it doesn't work, try Logistic Regression or SVM
```
